games.title: Cyberpunk 2020
games.note: Second edition of Mike Pondsmith's 1988 tabletop RPG Cyberpunk, set in the dark future of Night City.

games.title: Pathfinder Roleplaying Game
games.note: Paizo built it on the open rules of D&D 3.5, keeping it compatible with that edition's adventures.

games.title: Gothic
games.note: Set in a prison colony sealed under a magic barrier; it became a cult hit in Germany and Poland.

games.title: Gothic II
games.note: Picks up right after the first game, in and around the port town of Khorinis.

games.title: Risen
games.note: Piranha Bytes' first game after the Gothic name stayed with its former publisher.

games.title: Divine Divinity
games.note: Larian's first Divinity game, mixing Diablo-style action with a large open world; Swen Vincke directed and programmed it.

games.title: Disco Elysium
games.note: There is no combat: your 24 skills speak as voices in your head, and failed checks still move the story.

games.title: Zero Parades: For Dead Spies
games.note: ZA/UM's espionage RPG, released in May 2026 in the narrative and art style of Disco Elysium.

games.title: Pathfinder: Kingmaker
games.note: Adapts Paizo's six-part Kingmaker campaign and adds a kingdom for you to rule between adventures.

games.title: Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous
games.note: A crusade against demons, with 'mythic paths' that can turn you into an angel, a lich or a demon.

games.title: Cyberpunk 2077
games.note: Mike Pondsmith, creator of the tabletop game, consulted on the story and voices a radio DJ in it.

games.title: Starfield
games.note: Todd Howard called it 'Skyrim in space'; its look was nicknamed 'NASA-punk'.

games.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance
games.note: A medieval RPG with no magic or monsters, set in Bohemia in 1403.

games.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
games.note: Released in February 2025, it picks up directly where the first game ended; Daniel Vávra was creative director.

games.title: Mafia
games.note: Written and designed by Daniel Vávra; it recreates a 1930s American city called Lost Heaven.

games.title: Dragon's Dogma
games.note: Players climb onto giant monsters and hire 'pawns', AI companions created by other players.

games.title: Dragon's Dogma 2
games.note: A direct sequel released 12 years after the original, again directed by Hideaki Itsuno.

games.title: Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning
games.note: Lore by R. A. Salvatore and art by Todd McFarlane; 38 Studios collapsed months after release.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
games.note: Runs Oblivion's original Gamebryo game logic underneath new Unreal Engine 5 graphics.

games.title: Fallout 76
games.note: Bethesda's first online Fallout, set in West Virginia; human NPCs arrived only with the 2020 Wastelanders update.

links.took: The first game's bleak, oppressive mood, which Bethesda used as its model.
links.added: First-person open-world exploration of ruined Washington, D.C., with V.A.T.S. targeting.
links.extra: Lead designer Emil Pagliarulo preferred the first game's tone to Fallout 2's jokier dialogue.

links.took: Bethesda's Oblivion team, tools and open-world structure; fans joked it was 'Oblivion with guns'.
links.added: Guns, V.A.T.S. slow-motion targeting and a nuclear wasteland around Washington, D.C.
links.extra: The team grew after Oblivion shipped in 2006; both games run on the Gamebryo engine.

links.took: Burnout's slow-motion crash replays, which inspired V.A.T.S.'s slow-motion kill shots.
links.added: Used that cinematic slow motion for pause-and-target combat in an RPG.
links.extra: Wikipedia credits the Burnout series in general; Burnout 3 stands in for it here.

links.took: Black Isle veterans at Obsidian, whose cancelled Fallout 3, Van Buren, was also set around Nevada.
links.added: Faction reputation, multiple endings and a Mojave Desert built on Fallout 3's engine.
links.extra: Wikipedia: 'Fallout: New Vegas began with the cancellation of Van Buren.' Josh Sawyer directed it.

links.took: Fallout 3's codebase, which Bethesda forked to build the Creation Engine for Skyrim.
links.added: Hand-made dungeons, dragons and a Nordic land in place of a nuclear wasteland.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

links.extra: The developers called Skyrim a spiritual successor to both Fallout 3 and the earlier Elder Scrolls games.

links.took: The 'wonder of discovery' that Todd Howard wanted to recapture from Morrowind.
links.added: A distinct Nordic culture, dragon shouts and 150 hand-built dungeons.

links.took: The classic European fantasy of Arena and Daggerfall, which Oblivion returned to after Morrowind.
links.added: Radiant AI daily routines for townspeople, full voice acting and Havok physics.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion

links.extra: Skyrim's Wikipedia article says Oblivion went back to Arena and Daggerfall's classic fantasy at the cost of a unique culture.

links.took: Western fantasy tropes and the aim of a pen-and-paper RPG on a computer.
links.added: An alien island of giant mushrooms, Dark Elf houses and a living god.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind

links.extra: Todd Howard has said every Elder Scrolls game aims to resemble a pen-and-paper RPG.

links.took: The Creation Engine built for Skyrim, plus Bethesda's open-world design.
links.added: Settlement building, weapon crafting and a voiced hero in post-war Boston.

links.took: Bethesda's open-world RPG formula; Todd Howard described Starfield as 'Skyrim in space'.
links.added: Space travel, ship building and procedurally generated planets in a 'NASA-punk' setting.

links.took: Bethesda's team and tools; full development began after Fallout 4 shipped in 2015.
links.added: Creation Engine 2, rebuilt to handle procedurally generated planets.

links.took: Fallout 4's engine, crafting and settlement building.
links.added: An online world in West Virginia shared with other players.

links.took: Ken Rolston, Morrowind's lead designer who oversaw Oblivion's team, became its lead designer.
links.added: Fast, combo-based action combat and lore by fantasy author R. A. Salvatore.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion

links.took: Oblivion's original game logic, still running on its Gamebryo engine.
links.added: New Unreal Engine 5 graphics drawn on top of the old systems.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion

links.took: A huge open world you can explore in any direction from the start.
links.added: Physics-driven climbing, gliding and chemistry instead of RPG stats and dialogue.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

links.extra: Skyrim's Wikipedia article says developers credited it as an influence on Breath of the Wild, without naming them.

links.took: Skyrim's success with very large open-world fantasy RPGs.
links.added: A story-driven open world where side quests get the same care as the main plot.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

links.extra: Wikipedia credits Skyrim with popularizing big fantasy open worlds, influencing The Witcher and Dragon Age.

links.took: Reviewers compared it to a Skyrim stripped of magic and monsters.
links.added: Real 1403 Bohemia, demanding sword combat and needs such as sleep and food.
links.extra: A critic's comparison (GameRevolution), not a developer statement.

links.took: Daniel Vávra, Mafia's writer and designer, who later co-founded Warhorse.
links.added: A first-person medieval RPG grounded in historical research.
links.extra: Vávra went on to lead both Kingdom Come games.

links.took: Henry's story, which continues directly from the first game's ending.
links.added: A larger world including the city of Kuttenberg, and deeper combat.

links.took: Named a 'major influence' by executive producer Martin Klíma.
links.added: Medieval Bohemia in place of fantasy, with realistic combat and survival needs.

src.t: Wikipedia: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II (cites Martin Klíma)

links.took: Design influences cited by design director Viktor Bocan.
links.added: Realistic medieval swordplay with directional attacks and timed counters.

src.t: Wikipedia: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II (cites Viktor Bocan)

links.extra: Bocan cited the Dark Souls series together with Elden Ring.

links.took: Design influences cited by design director Viktor Bocan.
links.added: A historical open world with no magic or monsters.

src.t: Wikipedia: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II (cites Viktor Bocan)

links.took: The Witcher 3's quest system and its 'quest twist' philosophy, plus CD Projekt's REDengine.
links.added: A first-person open city, Night City, with cyberware and different life paths.

links.took: Mike Pondsmith's setting, which CD Projekt licensed from the year 2077 onward.
links.added: A first-person open-world RPG; Pondsmith consulted on the story.

links.took: The first Deus Ex was one of the art team's inspirations.
links.added: An open city where most jobs can be done by stealth, hacking or force.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the art team drew on the first Deus Ex, System Shock and Ghost in the Shell.

links.took: Its third-person action RPG design in a gritty fantasy world.
links.added: Andrzej Sapkowski's monster hunter Geralt and choices with delayed consequences.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Witcher (developers cited Gothic as a primary influence)

links.extra: CD Projekt had published Gothic in Poland, where it was very popular.

links.took: The nameless hero, the factions and Gothic's harsh learning curve.
links.added: A much larger world around the port town of Khorinis.

links.took: Piranha Bytes' open-world design: factions, a nameless hero and tough early combat.
links.added: A new volcanic island setting, since the Gothic name stayed with its old publisher.

src.t: Wikipedia: Gothic (calls Risen a similar game by the same developer)

links.took: A modified version of BioWare's Aurora engine from Neverwinter Nights.
links.added: Timing-based sword combat, potion alchemy and Sapkowski's Slavic-flavored world.

links.took: Ultima VII's freely interactive world; Swen Vincke says no RPG since has done it better.
links.added: Turn-based tactical combat, elemental combos and two-player co-op.

src.t: Swen Vincke, PC Gamer (Jeremy Peel), Dec 2020

links.extra: Vincke: 'Everything out there after Ultima 7 never did it as good as Ultima 7.'

links.took: A living, object-filled world in the style of Ultima VII.
links.added: Diablo-like real-time combat and a skill system later Divinity games kept.

src.t: Swen Vincke, PC Gamer (Jeremy Peel), Dec 2020

links.extra: PC Gamer says Vincke is determined to put a little bit of Ultima 7 into every Larian game.

links.took: Diablo's real-time, click-to-attack action and loot.
links.added: A large open world with quests, crafting and classless skills.
links.extra: Wikipedia notes 'significant similarities to Diablo' without citing a developer.

links.took: The Divinity world of Rivellon and its skill system.
links.added: A prequel with turn-based combat and chain reactions between elements.

links.took: Larian's engine, turn-based combat and elemental surfaces from Original Sin II.
links.added: D&D 5th edition rules and cinematic, fully voiced conversations.

links.took: The 5th edition D&D rules and the Forgotten Realms.
links.added: On-screen dice rolls for skill checks during conversations.

links.took: An amnesiac hero, dialogue over combat and painted isometric scenes.
links.added: Skills that talk back as voices in your head, in a decaying modern city.

src.t: Wikipedia: Disco Elysium (cites Robert Kurvitz's pitch and a ZA/UM Steam post, 2020)

links.took: The isometric party RPG; Kurvitz pitched his game as a modern advance on Baldur's Gate.
links.added: No combat at all, with failure treated as part of the story.

src.t: Wikipedia: Disco Elysium (cites Robert Kurvitz's pitch)

links.took: Open, reactive role-playing; Kurvitz called his game 'from the Fallout school of RPG'.
links.added: A detective story where your politics and inner voices shape the case.
links.extra: The remark comes from a Kurvitz livestream, according to Wikipedia.

links.took: Kurvitz pitched 'D&D meets '70s cop-show'; his group first made a D&D-based tabletop game.
links.added: A detective RPG set in an original 'fantastic realist' world.

src.t: Wikipedia: Disco Elysium (cites Robert Kurvitz's pitch)

links.extra: Wikipedia says Kurvitz's teenage D&D games shaped the game's acceptance of failure.

links.took: ZA/UM's narrative design and painted art style.
links.added: A spy story, made after Disco Elysium's lead designer Robert Kurvitz had left the studio.

links.took: The D&D 3.5 System Reference Document, released under the Open Game License.
links.added: Revised classes and rules that stayed compatible with 3.5 adventures.

links.took: Pathfinder first edition rules and Paizo's six-part Kingmaker campaign.
links.added: A pausable real-time CRPG with kingdom management between adventures.

links.took: Systems from classic CRPGs such as Baldur's Gate: pausable party combat in isometric view.
links.added: Pathfinder's dense rules and a kingdom to build and govern.

links.took: Systems from classic D&D CRPGs, Neverwinter Nights among them.
links.added: A long Pathfinder campaign with kingdom building.

links.took: Owlcat's engine, Pathfinder rules and pausable party combat.
links.added: Mythic paths that transform your hero, adapting the Wrath of the Righteous campaign.

links.took: Classic fantasy monsters and adventuring; Hideaki Itsuno cited D&D as an inspiration for the world.
links.added: Climbing onto giant monsters and AI 'pawn' companions shared between players.
links.extra: Itsuno also named The Lord of the Rings and The Neverending Story.

links.took: A Western-style open fantasy world to roam.
links.added: Devil May Cry-style action combat and climbing on monsters.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the team aimed to emulate Western RPGs such as Oblivion, Fallout 3 and Fable II.

links.took: Controls and action combat carried over by staff who had worked on Devil May Cry.
links.added: An open-world RPG with vocations and a party of pawns.

links.took: Pawns, vocations and monster climbing.
links.added: A larger world with two kingdoms and a disease that spreads between pawns.
